# Part I: Foundations {.unnumbered .part}

Four chapters stand between you and the first project: one for the Publish step of the loop,
one for Prompt and Check, one for the machine that runs them all, and one in which you use
that machine by hand.

**Chapter 1, Publishing That Rebuilds Itself.** Why hand-made reports drift out of date, and
how Quarto rebuilds every output from one source so that they cannot. You will follow one
file through the three steps of a render, learn exactly what "reproducible" promises, and see
when Quarto is the wrong tool.

**Chapter 2, Working With a Coding Agent.** What an agent is, what it costs, how far
its reach goes, and how to ask it for work you can verify. You will learn to read the
book's hands-on boxes, and how to account for an agent's use when the work is research.

**Chapter 3, Setting Up Your Machine.** Six steps, each with a check you can see, from an
empty terminal to a working agent, Quarto and Python. It ends when a web page and a PDF
that your own computer built both say 42.

**Chapter 4, A First Report, by Hand.** A one-page report with a wrong number in it, which
renders without an error. You copy it, render it and find the wrong number by checking the
report against its data. Then you record it with Git, change the data and undo the change,
and read three errors made on purpose. Only then does the agent make its first edit, and you
check its diff before you commit it.

The first two chapters are mostly reading. The last two are hands-on: do them at a desk, with
a good connection, about an hour for the setup and about 45 minutes for the first report.

Its chapters: 1, Publishing That Rebuilds Itself, where you read why one source beats copies; 2, Working With a Coding Agent, how to ask for work and check it; 3, Setting Up Your Machine, where you build a computer that renders the test run; 4, A First Report, by Hand, where you build a report you checked, fixed and committed."}
